hook: Did you know 1818 brought the birth of a daring spy operating right out of Richmond, Virginia?

sections.voiceover: Did you know 1818 brought the birth of a daring spy operating right out of Richmond, Virginia?

sections.voiceover: Van Lew entered the world on October 12, 1818, in Richmond, and died there in 1900.
sections.visual_cue: Archival map of Richmond showing Libby Prison and Shockhoe Cemetery.

sections.voiceover: Except Van Lew didn't stop there, aiding Union officers imprisoned in Libby Prison during the war's first two years.
sections.visual_cue: Close up shot of handwritten 19th-century correspondence documents.
sections.sfx_cue: Paper rustling and scratching quill pen sound.
sections.animation_cue: Slight push-in on the handwritten text.

sections.voiceover: Starting in 1861, Elizabeth Van Lew sent warning letters to the Union War Department. She transmitted vital intelligence straight from Richmond to the Union War Department.
sections.visual_cue: Historic photograph of the Union War Department building in Washington.
sections.sfx_cue: Telegraph machine ticking out a coded message.
b_roll: Union War Department historical building photograph
sections.animation_cue: Slow zoom in toward the center of the historic building image.

sections.voiceover: Visit Shockhoe Cemetery in Richmond to see her grave.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic shot of the gravestone marker at Shockhoe Cemetery.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft wind chime and ambient church bells.
sections.animation_cue: Slow pan upward along the weathered stone marker.
